label: prf:spectral-decomposition-qvalue
title: Proof of spectral decomposition qvalue
html:
Proof sketch

  1. Completeness. The Rosso–Jones formula decomposes J_{\tau(r,s)}(q) = \sum_{\lambda \vdash r} d_\lambda(q) \cdot \omega_\lambda^s into irreps of H_r(q). Every irrep \lambda is recoverable from the torus knot data by Möbius inversion on the power sums \omega^s. The self-duality \tau(r,s) \leftrightarrow \tau(s,r) provides the required inner product. Thus, \mathcal{E}_g spans the representation ring at each degree \leq \lfloor 2g/(g-1) \rfloor.

  2. Inductive chain construction. We add each nucleon k by extending the 2\!\times\!2 chain matrices: M_j \leftarrow M_j \cdot T_{j {}^j\!\bowtie_k k}(q) for existing positions j < k, and M_{k-1} = T_{(k\!-\!1) {}^{k-1}\!\bowtie_k k}(q) for the new position. The Hecke reduction \sigma^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma + 1 acts strictly within each 2\!\times\!2 chain. This demands zero Yang–Baxter steps and zero Hecke steps on the multi-generator element. The nuclear word \mathcal{N}_{Z,N} = \prod_j (\mathfrak{w}^+_j \sigma_j + \mathfrak{w}^0_j) employs distinct generators, ensuring it remains in Gröbner--Shirshov normal form.

  3. Shell cancellation. The parent and daughter nuclei share all chains except those traversing the converting nucleon. The log ratio \log_q(P_{\mathrm{dau}}/P_{\mathrm{par}}) = \sum_j [\log_q \hat{V}_j^{\mathrm{dau}} - \log_q \hat{V}_j^{\mathrm{par}}] therefore accumulates contributions only from generators j that explicitly interact with the converting nucleon.

  4. Pauli projection. A fully occupied shell of n fermions is completely antisymmetric. Under the Schur–Weyl decomposition of H_3(q), the decay operator T_{\beta\text{-decay}}(q) projects onto the alternating irrep (1^3) via e_{(1^3)} \cdot T_{\beta\text{-decay}}(q) \cdot e_{(1^3)}. The symmetric and standard irreps cancel entirely in the fully occupied state.

  5. Tower termination. The degree-k tower knot \tau(r, s^k) demands genus (r-1)(s^k - 1)/2. For g = 4: degree 1 admits 4 knots, degree 2 admits 2 knots (\tau(2,9) and \tau(3,4)), and degree 3 requires genus \geq 13. Consequently, the jet bundle over \Sigma_4 possesses exactly three non-zero levels (k = 0, 1, 2).

Degree-1 knots are already encoded in \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{bare}} through distinct vertex weights (\mathfrak{p} {}^i\!\oplus_j \mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{n} {}^i\!\oplus_j \mathfrak{n}, \mathfrak{p} {}^i\!\oplus_j \mathfrak{n} — inter-particle Hopf links with crossing indices i, j), so F = 1 for shells 1–4. The active correction comes from degree-2 knots only.

Jet bundle structure

The knot operators form a jet bundle over the exceptional divisor chain of \Sigma_g. The jet index is the Gröbner--Shirshov class (the degree in the degree tower) of each torus knot.

See Table 2.

The jet decomposition is exact and finite. This finiteness arises not from truncation, but from the finite dimensionality of the regular representation of H_n(q) on \Sigma_g. Completeness follows from the self-duality \tau(r,s) \leftrightarrow \tau(s,r) and the Rosso–Jones expansion. Every irrep of H_n(q) is recoverable from the torus knot invariants. Consequently, the knots form a complete orthogonal basis under the Markov trace inner product.

Shell correction proportions

The product \prod F(\tau, N) reduces to two categorically defined proportions for shells \geq 5 (N > 28).

Degree-2 shell factor (F_{\mathrm{deg2}}). For shells at degree 2 in the torus knot tower, the two embeddable degree-2 knots \tau(2,9) and \tau(3,4) contribute a Rosso--Jones weighted average:

  F_{\mathrm{deg2}}
  = \frac{
      J(\tau(2,9)) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\tau(2,9) \cdot \Delta_\beta)
    + J(\tau(3,4)) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\tau(3,4) \cdot \Delta_\beta)
    }{
      \bigl(J(\tau(2,9)) + J(\tau(3,4))\bigr)
      \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\Delta_\beta)
    }
  \approx 0.5904,

where J(\tau(r,s)) = \sum_{\lambda \vdash r} d_\lambda(q) \cdot \omega_\lambda^s is the Rosso--Jones invariant. This is the quantum-dimension weighted trace of the full twist on each irrep of H_r(q). The operator \Delta_\beta = T_{\mathrm{mix}} - T_{nn} is the beta-decay difference operator. The Rosso--Jones weights form the canonical inner product on R(H_r(q)). Schur orthogonality forces this structure. They assign each degree-2 knot its Rosso--Jones invariant J(\tau) with zero fitting freedom.

At q = q_0, J(\tau(2,9)) \approx 2.167 and J(\tau(3,4)) \approx 5.794. This is computed from the Rosso--Jones expansion J(\tau(r,s)) = \sum_\lambda d_\lambda(q_0)\omega_\lambda^s. Therefore, \tau(3,4) receives approximately 2.67\times the weight of \tau(2,9).

Kummer tower decomposition. The two degree-2 knots correspond to the prime factorisation of the Euler characteristic |\chi(A)| = 6 = 2 \times 3 through the Kummer tower filtration (Kummer filtration):

  • \tau(3,4) has s = 4 = 2^2. This is the \mu_2 branch of the Kummer tower (even/odd parity).
  • \tau(2,9) has s = 9 = 3^2. This is the \mu_3 branch (threefold symmetry).

The Chinese Remainder Theorem decomposition \mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z} \cong \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z} produces exactly these two independent components. The Rosso--Jones weights are the quantum dimensions of the corresponding Kummer components. We find J(\tau(3,4)) > J(\tau(2,9)) because the \mu_2 component (parity) possesses a larger quantum dimension in the degree-2 representation ring than the \mu_3 component (threefold symmetry).

Pauli exclusion factor (F_{\mathrm{Pauli}}). For magic-number neutron shells (N \in \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\}), the filled shell projects onto the alternating irrep (1^3) via the Young symmetrizer e_{(1^3)}:

  F_{\mathrm{Pauli}}
  = \frac{|\mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{alt}}(\Delta_\beta)|}
         {|\mathrm{tr}(\Delta_\beta)|}
  = \frac{|\lambda_{\mathrm{alt}}|}{|\lambda_{\mathrm{sym}}|}
  \approx 0.6382,

where \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{alt}} evaluates each Hecke word w with eigenvalue (-q^{-1})^{\ell(w)} (alternating channel) and \mathrm{tr} uses q^{\ell(w)} (symmetric channel). This evaluates the ratio of alternating to symmetric eigenvalues of \Delta_\beta in the 6 \times 6 regular representation of H_3(q).

Combined formula. For a \beta^- decay with the converting neutron in shell degree d and neutron occupation parity p:

  Q
  = \mathcal{Q}_{\mathrm{bare}}
    \times F_{\mathrm{deg2}}^{[d \geq 2]}
    \times F_{\mathrm{Pauli}}^{[N \in \mathrm{magic}]},

where [\cdot] is the Iverson bracket. The combined proportion F_{\mathrm{deg2}} \times F_{\mathrm{Pauli}} = 0.5904 \times 0.6382 \approx 0.377 applies to magic-number nuclei in heavy shells. An example is {}^{137}\mathrm{Cs} with N = 82.
